content: This medication is specifically used to treat bacterial eye infections. It is not effective for other types of eye infections. Instructions for Use: 1. Before Use: Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting azithromycin and each time you get a refill. 2. Preparation: Wash your hands thoroughly before applying the eye drops. Do not wear contact lenses while using this medication or if you have a bacterial eye infection. 3. First-Time Use: If this is your first time using the medication, hold the dropper upright and remove the cap to release any extra pressure in the dropper. 4. Before Each Use: Shake the dropper once while holding it upside down. Then, remove the cap while keeping the dropper in the same position. 5. Application: Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly over your eye and place one drop into the pouch. Look downward and gently close your eyes for 1 to 2 minutes. Place one finger at the corner of your eye near the nose and apply gentle pressure to prevent the medication from draining out. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eye. 6. Using Other Eye Medications: If you are using other eye medications (drops or ointments), wait at least 5 to 10 minutes before applying them. 7. Consistency: Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. To help you remember, use it at the same time(s) each day. 8. Duration: Continue using the medication for the full duration prescribed by your doctor, even if symptoms improve earlier. Side Effects: Temporary eye irritation, stinging, burning, or blurred vision may occur. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to other types of eye infections, including fungal infections. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms of a severe allergic reaction. Precautions: Inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to azithromycin, other macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin, clarithromycin), ketolide antibiotics (e.g., telithromycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. After applying the medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred. Avoid driving or operating machinery until your vision clears. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if azithromycin passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone swallows this medication and experiences serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Storage: Store unopened bottles in the refrigerator. Once opened, the bottle can be stored in the refrigerator or at room temperature. However, the medication expires 14 days after opening. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Important Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor. Discard any unused medication after completing the treatment or after 14 days from opening. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
